############################################################ SPORTS
############################################################ BULLS SLIP TO 28-13: STILL BEST IN EAST, BUT MOMENTUM QUESTIONS EMERGE Two-game losing streak follows historic start By Selena Grant | Bay Tribune Chicago Bureau CHICAGO — The Bulls dropped to 28-13 after consecutive losses this week, their first back-to-back defeats since early in the season. The losses — both to Western Conference opponents on a road trip — don’t fundamentally alter Chicago’s position atop the Eastern Conference, but they’ve prompted questions about the team’s depth and sustainability. Josh Giddey continues to anchor the offense with 16.7 points, 7.1 rebounds, and 6.2 assists per game. Hank Trepagnier remains productive in the frontcourt with 16 points and 7.7 rebounds. But the bench, which carried Chicago through the NBA Cup run, has shown inconsistency in recent games.

============================================================ CULTURE & COMMUNITY
============================================================ THEO BANKS PERFORMS AT KEANE GALA — TRAJECTORY CONTINUES By Kai Marston | Bay Tribune Arts
Trepagnier, the 21-year-old center from El Salvador, has become the face of Chicago's unexpected ascent. His matchup against Wembanyama — the generational prospect everyone assumed would dominate the conversation — tilted Chicago's way. Trepagnier finished with four rebounds, a block, and the kind of defensive presence that forced San Antonio into contested shots all night. Josh Giddey orchestrated from the point: 16 points, seven rebounds, 12 assists. The near-triple-double has become routine. The Bulls sit at 9-1. Team chemistry has climbed to 77%. Fan interest hovers near 56% — numbers that would have seemed absurd in October. "This is what development looks like," Mike Paulson said after the game, his first public appearance since the Chicago presser where he addressed the Oakland walkout. "We built the system. They're executing it." Paulson watched from his courtside seat, phone in hand, already fielding texts about spring training in Mesa. The GM who runs two franchises sat in Chicago while his baseball team prepared for Arizona without him.
